faqs.q: How is overtime paid for a civil engineer under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Professional Employees Award, overtime hours (over 38 per week or an agreed average) are paid at the ordinary minimum hourly rate, not time‑and‑a‑half. However, once your annual salary is 25% or more above the minimum for your classification, the overtime clauses no longer apply. For a Level 1 graduate (pay point 1.1), that threshold is $85,672.50. faqs.q: What is the casual loading for a civil engineer?
faqs.a: A casual civil engineer must be paid a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 1 graduate (4‑year degree) the casual rate is $43.21 per hour ($34.57 × 1.25). This loading compensates for entitlements casuals do not receive, such as paid leave. The loading is paid on all hours worked, including penalty rates if applicable.

faqs.q: How much super is paid on a civil engineer salary?
faqs.a: Employers must contribute superannuation at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the salary. For a graduate on $68,538, that adds about $8,225 per year. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). Contributions are not deducted from your take‑home pay; they are an additional benefit.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Civil Engineer Salary in Australia

If you are a civil engineer or considering the profession, knowing the legal minimums and typical earnings helps you negotiate with confidence. The **civil engineer salary** is governed by the Professional Employees Award 2020 (MA000065), which sets minimum annual wages and hourly rates for classifications from graduate to experienced professional. This article explains how to convert those rates to weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, and what you can expect after tax and super.

### Award Minimum Rates for Civil Engineers

Under the award, a graduate civil engineer with a 4‑ or 5‑year degree recognised by Engineers Australia must be paid at least **$68,538 per year** as of 1 July 2026. That equates to **$34.57 per hour** for a 38‑hour week. The award also defines higher levels:

| Classification | Annual wage | Hourly rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 Graduate (pay point 1.1) | $68,538 | $34.57 |
| Level 2 Experienced professional | $78,836 | $39.77 |
| Level 3 Professional | $86,157 | $43.46 |
| Level 4 Professional | $97,173 | $49.02 |

These rates come directly from. The hourly rate is calculated as (annual wage × 6/313) ÷ 38. For a full‑time employee, ordinary hours are 38 per week.

### How the Civil Engineer Salary Compares to the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Even the lowest graduate civil engineer rate of $34.57 is 31% above the national minimum. This reflects the professional qualifications and skills required.

For casual employees, the award adds a 25% loading. A casual graduate civil engineer earns **$43.21 per hour** ($34.57 × 1.25). The National Minimum Wage casual rate is $33.05. You can read more about [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) on our site.

### Typical Earnings: Median and Average Civil Engineer Salary

According to the Australian Taxation Office’s 2023–24 tax returns, the median salary or wage income for civil engineers was **$120,000**, and the average was **$131,274**. Jobs and Skills Australia reports median full‑time weekly earnings of **$2,217** (about $59 per hour) for Civil Engineering Professionals, compared to $1,852 for all occupations. These figures show that many civil engineers earn well above the award minimum.

### Converting Hourly Rates to Annual, Fortnightly, and Take‑Home Pay

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a graduate on $34.57/hour working 38 hours:
$34.57 × 38 × 52 = $68,538 (matching the award).

For the median $120,000 salary, the equivalent hourly rate is about $60.73 (assuming 38 hours).

**Fortnightly pay** is simply weekly pay × 2. For the graduate minimum, weekly pay is $1,313.83, so fortnightly is $2,627.66 before tax.

### Tax and Medicare on a Civil Engineer Salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (no surcharge assumed).

On the $68,538 graduate salary, tax and Medicare total about **$12,452**, leaving take‑home pay of **$56,086 per year** ($2,157 per fortnight).

On the median $120,000, tax and Medicare are about **$28,920**, leaving **$91,080 per year** ($3,503 per fortnight).

See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed breakdown.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must contribute superannuation at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a graduate on $68,538, that’s an extra **$8,225 per year** into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is paid on top. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### When Overtime and Penalty Rates Apply

Under the award, hours beyond 38 per week (or an agreed average) are paid at the ordinary hourly rate, not at a premium. However, if your annual salary is 25% or more above the minimum for your classification, the overtime and penalty clauses no longer apply. For a Level 1 graduate, that threshold is $85,672.50. Above that, your contract determines overtime arrangements.

### Summary

The civil engineer salary ranges from the award minimum of $68,538 for a graduate to well over $100,000 for experienced professionals. Use the hourly rate × 38 × 52 formula to convert any offer. Remember that super is on top, and tax depends on your total income. For more information, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

*Disclaimer: Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.*
